ukmt-sk-2016-01.title: Use the pattern
ukmt-sk-2016-01.body:
The picture shows that the sum of the first $n$ odd numbers is $n\times n$. The sum has $11$ terms (the 11th odd number is $21$), so it equals $11\times11=121$.

**Answer: 121**

ukmt-sk-2016-01.title: Pair up
ukmt-sk-2016-01.body:
Pair the terms from the ends: $1+21=22$, $3+19=22$, $\dots$, five pairs, plus the middle term $11$: $5\times22+11=121$.

**Answer: 121**

ukmt-sk-2016-02.title: Compare columns
ukmt-sk-2016-02.body:
In each of the first ten columns the lower number is $10$ more than the upper one, so the lower row's first ten entries sum to $100$ more than the upper row's. To make the rows equal, $*$ must be $100$ less than $1050$, i.e. $950$.

**Answer: 950**

ukmt-sk-2016-03.title: Compare volumes
ukmt-sk-2016-03.body:
The cubes have edges $2$ dm and $6$ dm, so volumes $8\text{ dm}^3$ and $216\text{ dm}^3$. Since $216\div8=27$ exactly, $27$ full trips are needed (and suffice).

**Answer: 27**

ukmt-sk-2016-05.title: Find the vertices
ukmt-sk-2016-05.body:
The graphs meet where $2|x|-3=|x|$, i.e. $|x|=3$, at $(\pm3,3)$. The graphs have their vertices at $(0,-3)$ and $(0,0)$. The enclosed region is the triangle with vertices $(-3,3),(3,3),(0,-3)$ (area $\frac12\cdot6\cdot6=18$) with the triangle $(-3,3),(3,3),(0,0)$ (area $\frac12\cdot6\cdot3=9$) removed: $18-9=9$.

**Answer: 9**

ukmt-sk-2016-06.title: Angle chase
ukmt-sk-2016-06.body:
The radii $OT$, $OS$ are perpendicular to the tangents, so in quadrilateral $PTOS$ we get $\angle TPS=360^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ-150^\circ=30^\circ$. Hence $\angle TPY=30^\circ-10^\circ=20^\circ$. In triangle $PTY$ the other two angles sum to $180^\circ-20^\circ=160^\circ$.

**Answer: 160**

ukmt-sk-2016-07.title: Edges of a prism
ukmt-sk-2016-07.body:
If the base is an $N$-gon, the prism has $N$ edges on each of two bases and $N$ vertical edges: $3N$ edges. The multiples of $3$ strictly between $310$ and $320$ are $312,315,318$, and only $315$ is odd.

**Answer: 315**

ukmt-sk-2016-08.title: Each bracket is zero
ukmt-sk-2016-08.body:
A sum of squares is zero only if each term is zero, so $x=\pm3$, $y=\pm2$, $z=\pm1$. The sum $x+y+z$ is even (odd+even+odd), lies between $-6$ and $6$, and each even value $-6,-4,\dots,6$ occurs (changing one sign changes the sum by $2$, $4$ or $6$; e.g. $3+2+1=6$, $3+2-1=4$, $3-2+1=2$, $3-2-1=0$, $-3+2-1=-2$, $-3-2+1=-4$, $-3-2-1=-6$). So there are $7$ values.

**Answer: 7**

ukmt-sk-2016-09.title: Pythagoras
ukmt-sk-2016-09.body:
Let $R,r$ be the radii and $O$ the centre. The radius to the point of tangency is perpendicular to $AB$ and bisects it, so $R^2-r^2=16^2=256$. The shaded area is $\pi R^2-\pi r^2=256\pi$, so $k=256$.

**Answer: 256**

ukmt-sk-2016-10.title: Find the maximum
ukmt-sk-2016-10.body:
All stars as $\times$ gives $720$. Replacing any star other than the first by $+$ splits the product into two parts, each at most $360$ in total effect, which is smaller. Replacing only the first star gives $1+2\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot6=721$, the maximum. $721=7\times103$, so the largest prime factor is $103$.

**Answer: 103**

ukmt-sk-2016-11.title: Odd year and even year
ukmt-sk-2016-11.body:
The two years are one odd and one even.

Odd year: odd months $1,3,5,7,9,11$; odd days: $16$ in the 31-day months ($1,3,5,7$) and $15$ in the 30-day months ($9,11$): $4\cdot16+2\cdot15=94$.

Even year: even months $2,4,6,8,10,12$; even days: $15$ in $4,6,8,10,12$ (each has 30 or 31 days, giving $15$ even days) and $14$ in February: $5\cdot15+14=89$ (leap years give $14$ too, since 29 is odd).

Total $94+89=183$.

**Answer: 183**

ukmt-sk-2016-12.title: Use the circumcircle
ukmt-sk-2016-12.body:
A triangle inscribed in a circle is right-angled exactly when one side is a diameter. The regular 18-gon has $9$ diameters joining opposite vertices. For each diameter the third vertex can be any of the other $16$ vertices. Each right-angled triangle has exactly one diameter as hypotenuse, so there are $9\times16=144$.

**Answer: 144**

ukmt-sk-2016-13.title: Divisibility by 7
ukmt-sk-2016-13.body:
If $Y=p+q$ and $2p=5q$ then $2Y=2p+2q=7q$, so $7\mid2Y$, hence $7\mid Y$. Conversely, if $7\mid Y$, put $q=\frac{2Y}7$ and $p=Y-q=\frac{5Y}7$ (positive integers with $2p=5q$). So we count multiples of $7$ from $2000$ to $3000$: the first is $1995+7=2002$, the last $2996$, giving $\frac{2996-2002}7+1=143$.

**Answer: 143**

ukmt-sk-2016-14.title: Triangle inequality
ukmt-sk-2016-14.body:
With $x\le y$ and $xy=105$, $(x,y)\in\{(1,105),(3,35),(5,21),(7,15)\}$. The triangle inequality $13+x>y$ rules out the first three, leaving $(7,15)$: $13+7+15=35$.

**Answer: 35**

ukmt-sk-2016-15.title: Enclose in a rectangle
ukmt-sk-2016-15.body:
Let each small triangle have side $x$ and height $h$, so $\frac12xh=10$ and $xh=20$. The shaded triangle fits in a rectangle of width $4x$ and height $3h$ (area $12xh$) with one vertex at a corner of the rectangle and the other two on its sides. The three leftover right triangles have areas $\frac12\cdot4x\cdot2h=4xh$, $\frac12\cdot\frac x2\cdot3h=\frac34xh$ and $\frac12\cdot\frac{7x}2\cdot h=\frac74xh$, totalling $\frac{13}2xh$. So $K=12xh-\frac{13}2xh=\frac{11}2xh=110$.

**Answer: 110**

ukmt-sk-2016-17.title: Find an invariant
ukmt-sk-2016-17.body:
Each turn removes two numbers and adds their sum plus $1$, so the total of all numbers on the board increases by $1$ per turn. The count drops from $100$ to $1$, so there are $99$ turns. The initial total is $10(1+\dots+10)=550$, so the final number is $550+99=649$.

**Answer: 649**

ukmt-sk-2016-19.title: Filter the squares
ukmt-sk-2016-19.body:
We need primes $k^2-21$. If $k$ is odd, $k^2-21$ is even, so $k$ is even. If $3\mid k$ then $3\mid k^2-21$; if $7\mid k$ then $7\mid k^2-21$; so $k$ is not a multiple of $3$ or $7$. Three-digit values need $k^2\ge121$ and $k^2\le1020$: $k\in\{12,\dots,31\}$ even and coprime to $3$, $7$: $k=16,20,22,26$ giving $235,379,463,655$. $235$ and $655$ are multiples of $5$; $379$ and $463$ are prime. The mean is $\frac{379+463}2=421$.

**Answer: 421**

ukmt-sk-2016-20.title: Recurrence
ukmt-sk-2016-20.body:
Let $C(m)$ be the number of barcodes of width $m$. Remove the first black strip and the first white strip (widths $b,w\in\{1,2\}$): what remains is again a barcode (it starts with a black strip) of width $m-b-w$, valid for $m-b-w\ge1$. The total removed width is $2,3,3,4$ for $(b,w)=(1,1),(2,1),(1,2),(2,2)$, so for $m\ge5$:
$$C(m)=C(m-2)+2C(m-3)+C(m-4).$$
Starting values: $C(1)=C(2)=C(3)=1$, $C(4)=3$. Then $C(5)=4$, $C(6)=6$, $C(7)=11$, $C(8)=17$, $C(9)=27$, $C(10)=45$, $C(11)=72$, $C(12)=116$.

**Answer: 116**
